page: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark results indicate average performance in stress-ng single-core (1519.79) and multi-core (6053.66) CPU tests. Large-block memory bandwidth is average, reaching 71.99 GB/sec for read-only and 35.14 GB/sec for write operations. However, the instance shows weak performance in several areas, including a Geekbench single-core score of 965.0 and a multi-core score of 3252.0. Small-block cached memory bandwidth is weak at 235.89 GB/sec, and Passmark CPU encryption performance is poor at 543.57.

The c6g.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM64-native workloads due to its dedicated core allocation and low resource footprint. However, users face tradeoffs, such as the complete absence of local storage and a lack of advanced x86 vector instructions like AVX or AMX. Cryptographic acceleration is limited to AES, and the instance exhibits poor performance in LLM inference tasks, with a 135M model prompt processing speed of 145.31 tokens/sec.
This instance is suited for lightweight compute-focused workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations that do not require high memory density or local storage.
